text: In the coherent Ising machine (CIM), each Ising spin is physically encoded in what?
choices: The binary phase (0 or pi) of a degenerate optical parametric oscillator
The amplitude of a single photon
The polarization state of a laser pulse
The wavelength of a frequency-comb line
explanation: A CIM spin is the binary phase (0 or pi) of a degenerate optical parametric oscillator, which becomes phase-bistable above threshold, mapping the two phases to the spin values plus and minus one. The robustness comes precisely from using phase (protected by the parametric process's Z2 symmetry), not amplitude, polarization, or comb-line wavelength.
